text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/03/11 - Essay - 01
Buildings and streets form a city neighborhood.
Pexels · 21576133
Getting to know a city
There is more than one way to explore a neighbourhood. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two useful
starting points.
One reason is that walking slowly helps us notice details we usually miss. For instance, we stop to look at a doorway instead of
hurrying to the next landmark. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice
what is happening.
Another reason is that respecting local routines makes a visit more considerate. For example, we keep an entrance clear while taking
a photograph of the street. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that different people
may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Write guidance for someone who wants to explore a neighbourhood for the first time. Explain two useful choices and why they matter.
Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the situation;
discuss walking slowly helps us notice details we usually miss with an example; discuss respecting local routines makes a visit more
considerate with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
